what_happened: On a straight multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT and then RIGHT route command, the policy steered left away from the recorded path, which stayed in its lane. It crossed the left lanes while slowing from about 17.7 to 11.9 m/s and ended up off the road in the median at 6.6 s. A following car (actor 40) hit its rear at that same moment as it braked and left its lane.

On a clear multi-lane road with no vehicle ahead, the policy's planned path veered left at about 10 m/s from soon after handoff, while the recorded route went straight and then curved right. The ego crossed the lane lines and ran into the planted median toward the oncoming lanes, ending 3.7 m off the recorded path.

The road curves gently left, but the policy kept planning and driving almost straight at about 12–13 m/s. It drifted right across the right edge line onto the shoulder and sidewalk and went offroad at 6.5 s, about 2.7 m from where the human drove; the camera view was clean and no actors were nearby.

After handoff the ego drifted right out of its lane at about 15 m/s and kept going right past the edge line, onto the shoulder and into the roadside trees, even though the recorded path and the LEFT command led away to the left. It went offroad at 11.4 s, 7.5 m from the recording. Actor 96 touched the ego's rear at about 9.4 s, but the ego was already sliding right, and the shoulder was still clearly visible on camera at 10.4 s, so the policy steered itself off the road.

The road and route curved right (the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT), but the policy kept planning straight and slightly to the left. The ego left its lane and ran onto the landscaped median with trees at about 7 m/s, ending 6.5 m from the human's path. The camera view looked clean before the failure, and no other actor was involved.

The route command was LEFT, but the ego slowed from 5 to about 1 m/s in the rightmost lane, about 11 m off the recorded path. Actor 3 rear-ended it at about 9.9 s, and the ego then crept over the right road edge and went offroad at 11.9 s. The camera was already heavily smeared on the right (a ghosted truck) before the failure, which may have played a part, but the policy itself drifted right against the route.

On the highway with a RIGHT command, the ego slowed from about 23.5 to 14.4 m/s and steered right across the solid edge line, while the mapped road curved left. At 6.7 s it was past the right boundary of the mapped road, and the camera showed only vegetation ahead. The human's recorded path also goes right of the mapped lanes, probably onto an exit ramp that isn't in the map. The ego was 3.6 m off that path, so it either cut the exit early or the map is missing the ramp.

The route said LEFT, but the ego was slowing (6.8→1.9 m/s) in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane highway, about 11 m off the recorded path, and it crept over the right road edge at 11.0 s. It had already been in contact with actors 4 (front) and 2 (rear), and the camera view was badly smeared by a ghosted truck, so the run was already falling apart when it left the road.

After handoff, the policy's planned path kept bending left, away from the route, even as the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT. The ego drifted left across the lanes and off into the landscaped median near the tree by 7.6 s, about 7 m from the recorded trajectory. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

After handoff at 4.5 s the road bent gently left, but the ego kept going nearly straight at about 12–13 m/s. Its plan, the orange line on the map, stayed straight while the lane curved away, so the ego drifted right over the white edge line onto the shoulder and dirt next to the fence. It was 2.6 m off the recorded path when it went off-road at 6.4 s. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

On a highway that bends left, the policy held a straight heading at about 23 m/s, slowing to 14 m/s. It drifted across the right edge line onto the shoulder toward the guardrail and was counted offroad at 6.8 s, 3.8 m from the human's path; the camera view was clean before it left the road.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT (RIGHT by the last frame), the policy took over and planned a drift into the lane on its left. It moved over into that lane and hit actor 41, which was alongside it on the left. The vehicle ahead stayed about 17–20 m away the whole time, so it played no part. The camera view looked clean before the move.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT and later RIGHT, the policy drifted left out of its lane instead of following its planned path, which stayed in lane and then bore right. It moved into the next lane over and hit vehicle 41, which was driving alongside in that lane. The lead truck stayed about 18 m ahead the whole time, so the collision had nothing to do with it.

The route curved right (the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT), but the policy kept planning straight and slightly to the left. The ego slowed from about 10 to 7.5 m/s and drifted out of its lane, ending up on the landscaped median left of the road by 7.6 s, about 6.6 m from the recorded path. No other actors were close, and the camera view looked clean until the ego reached the median.

The road bends left (the command changes to LEFT), but after handoff the ego kept a nearly straight heading at about 12–13 m/s. It drifted right across the lane edge onto the shoulder and sidewalk by the fence, ending about 2.8 m from the recorded human path. There were no other actors nearby, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

The ego was in the rightmost highway lane at about 23 m/s with a RIGHT command. It drifted right across the solid edge line onto the shoulder. It slowed to 14.5 m/s but didn't steer back as the road bent gently left, so it ran off the right edge about 3.6 m from the recorded human path. The camera view was clean before it left the lane; the smearing only appears once it is on the verge.

The command was RIGHT and the planned route ran along the right side of a wide multi-lane road, but the ego steered left across every lane toward the far left edge. It slowed from 7.6 to 1.7 m/s and still went over the left boundary onto the grass at 8.9 s, 12.4 m from the recorded path. The camera smearing appears only after the ego was already well away from the recorded path, so it is more likely a result of the drift than its cause.

The road and route curved right (the command changed to RIGHT around 6 s), but the policy kept going straight and veered slightly left, ending up in the landscaped median with trees and shrubs about 7 m from the recorded path. It slowed from 13 to 8.5 m/s, but there was no actor nearby and the camera view stayed clean until the ego was already off the road.

Even though the route command was RIGHT, the ego went left, about 11 m from the recorded path, which was further right. Its planned path bent left and then ran straight. It kept going at about 5–6 m/s and drove off the drivable area on the left edge of the highway at 11.9 s. The earlier rear contact is a separate event, and the camera smearing comes from being far off the recorded path, not from a rendering fault that caused the failure.

After taking over at 4.5s, the policy kept a steady speed of about 10 m/s but steered steadily left, away from the planned path that ran straight and then bore right. It crossed the lane lines and ran onto the landscaped median between the two carriageways, ending about 3.7 m off the recorded human path; the camera view looked clean before it left the road.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path veered left away from the recorded straight path, and the ego drifted into the adjacent left lane. Its front struck the side of actor 41, which was travelling alongside in that lane.

Given a RIGHT command, the ego instead turned left, away from its route on the right. It ended up about 11 m off the recorded path, angled across the lanes on the left side and pointing at the curb and grass. It slowed to about 1 m/s while blocking the lane, and actor 32, coming down that lane, struck the ego's side.

After handoff, the ego drifted into the rightmost lane, about 8–11 m right of the recorded path, even though the route command was LEFT. It braked from 6.6 to 1.5 m/s and touched actor 4 ahead at 9.2 s (3.3 m gap), was rear-ended by actor 3 around 10.2 s, and then edged over the right road boundary at 11.2 s with a wobbling plan. Because the ego was so far off the recording, the camera view was badly smeared (a distorted truck filled the right side), but this happened because the policy had already drifted off course.

The road curves to the left, and the route command changed to LEFT, but the ego kept going straight at about 10 m/s and did not follow the curve. It crossed the right edge line onto the shoulder and sidewalk next to the fence, ending 3.3 m off the recorded path, with no other actors involved.

The policy took over at 4.6 s while driving straight on a highway at about 35 m/s. It then steered left across the lanes and braked hard (down to 22.8 m/s), while the recorded human path stayed straight and then bore right. By 6.3 s the ego had left the road on the left (median side), about 5 m from the human path, and the following car (actor 7) hit its rear because of the sudden braking and swerve.

On a straight multi-lane highway at about 17 m/s, the policy's planned path veered left right after handoff, away from the recorded route, which stays in the right lanes, and the route command was RIGHT. The ego cut across lanes to the left and slowed to about 12 m/s, then left the drivable area at the left edge by the median at 6.6 s, 4.5 m from the recorded path; a following vehicle also hit its rear at that moment.

The road curved right toward an intersection, and the route command switched to RIGHT, but the policy kept heading straight and slightly left. It slowed from about 24 to 17 m/s but drove onto the left median island, about 4.3 m off the recorded human path. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clear before the ego left the road.

After taking over, the ego swerved out of its lane toward the right road edge, turning almost sideways toward the curb and grass while slowing to about 1 m/s, about 12 m off the recorded path. It was stopped across the lane when replayed vehicle 32, coming down that lane, hit its side (a lateral collision).

On a multi-lane road with a LEFT route command, the ego sat in the rightmost lane about 10 m from where the human drove, and the camera view was badly smeared, with a ghost truck on the right. It braked steadily from 4.5 to 0.9 m/s, got rear-ended by actor 3 at about 10 s (not its fault), then slowly drifted right over the road edge and went offroad at 12 s.

On a straight multi-lane highway at about 15 m/s, the ego drifted right of the recorded path and toward the right road edge, and its planned path bent right while the command was STRAIGHT. Around 9.9s actor 96 hit its rear, and by 10.9s the ego had crossed the right boundary into the trees and went offroad (7.5 m off the recorded path), even though the command had become LEFT.

In slow highway traffic at about 3 m/s, the ego steered right out of its lane toward the next lane, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then LEFT. Its front hit actor 13, which was driving alongside in that lane. The recorded human stayed in the original lane, to the left.

On a highway curving left at about 16 m/s, with the command switching to LEFT, the ego kept going roughly straight instead of following the curve. It drifted across the right lanes and left the road over the right edge, about 7 m from the recorded path. The camera smeared on the right side as the ego moved away from the recorded drive, but the left curve of the road was still clearly visible.

With a STRAIGHT/RIGHT command, the ego drifted left out of its lane, away from the recorded path that kept to the right. It sideswiped actor 56, which was travelling alongside in the left lane (a lateral collision at 7.4 s while accelerating to 5.2 m/s). The lead vehicle stayed about 16 m ahead the whole time, so this was not a lead-vehicle problem.
